title: God as Provider and the Meaning of House and City
english: And females; there shall be from the winged ones according to their kind, and from the cattle according to kind, and from all creeping things of the earth according to their kinds... Two by two from all shall come in to you to be fed with you, male and female. And let one note that here 'kind' is used instead of 'species', it being said sometimes 'species' and 'kind'. [Gap] And you shall take to yourself from all the foods that you eat, and you shall gather to yourself, and there shall be for you and for them to eat.

It is to be supposed for the righteous man not only to think of himself and those with him, but also of the speechless, for he rightly pities the souls of his animals. Regarding 'gathering to yourself', it has a remark that in the places where you live, and other animals do not approach, gather the foods; for if they lay in those places, they were working out their need by greedily attacking the foods.

And Noah did all that the Lord God commanded him, so he did. It is praiseworthy when done with understanding, a reliable one capable of judging rightly says, 'that he did thus as the one who commanded had instructed him'; for this is the virtue of the action. For there was once [gap] not indeed thus as he was commanded; for [gap] to the showing of the action [gap] of the disposition, not the manner which is [gap]. Every action not occurring with the proper calculation is incomplete, even if the result becomes perfect; and the righteous is testified to as having also done [gap].

For this also the Savior instructs, saying, 'Have mercy and you shall be shown mercy' (Luke 6:36), but he intends that mercy should not come through pitying, which is not to be a merchant or to play with the needs of the suffering; for they say, 'Become perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect' (Matthew 5:48); for God is giving of Himself and not receiving from another; so also you, zeal for the giving, just as the blessed Paul also leaves [it]: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive' (Acts 20:35). For the one receiving does not imitate the...

God is not one who receives anything from anyone, but is the provider of all good things. Thus, the imitator of God gives. As it is written, 'And the Lord God said to Noah: Enter, you and all your household, into the ark, because I have seen you righteous before me in this generation' (Gen 7:1).

In this way it appears that the whole house consisted of only the eight; for they did not bring a healer unless it was to prevent men from being lost or because of the being of such people. Therefore, a house is called here the kinship within the eight, for often such a name is shared by those who are of the same kind, especially regarding the one having been built. The same thing you would find regarding a city.

For it is said in the Gospel, 'And he led him' (meaning Jesus), 'to the brow of the mountain, where their city was built' (Matt 13:52), signifying now the name of the city that was constructed and built; and in 'And when Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred' (Matt 21:10), the gathering of the people is signified by the city. And again, in 'Jesus began to upbraid the cities in which most of his powers had come to pass, because they did not repent' (Luke 19:43), this signifies: for repentance does not happen in non-living things or material things; whereas the name of the house signifies the building in 'This is this house...' [text gapped].

...the assembly, the gathering, if it is said... the royal, and the jailer, and the house. He says the reason for entering the ark was 'because I saw you righteous before me' (Gen 7:1). He did not say simply 'because I saw you'—for Abel was righteous and Enoch, whose hope was 'to call upon the name of the Lord God' (Heb 11:6)—but 'because I saw you righteous before me in this generation,' making it clear. It is not merely presented that because of his virtue and his children participating in it they were saved, but, as previously foretold, the generation signifies the likeness, just as we have set forth also in the cases of those who perished. It also signifies the generation of the same manner, to say 'all righteous blood shed upon the earth from the...'

title: Common Notion and Numerical Symbolism
english: In the generation of the righteous, so that we might take the righteous with him, he himself was found righteous against [the world], not being entirely righteous against God being righteous; for only sons and women were found righteous against Noah. But it is great thus to be the opposite of God to be called righteous, as it is said: 'And the stars are not pure before him' (Job 9:21) and the other lights; but also in the psalms it is said: 'No living thing shall be justified before you' (Psalm 5:4), and again another saying he says: 'All our righteousness was as a garment laid aside' (Isaiah 64:6) from the presence of all the righteous.

From the clean animals he brought into the ark seven male and female, and from the animals not being clean two two  and female, and from the birds of the heaven the clean seven seven male and female, and from the birds not being clean two male and female, to breed seed upon all the earth. Consequently, even seven' (Genesis 7:2) he commands to be brought in from the clean. Since they were for food and for religious services for men, and they themselves who remained in the ark had need, therefore more are taken, so that from them and a greater generation might arise a succession suitable for their needs; but concerning the others, having brought in this many, he commanded 'two' (Genesis 7:2) to be brought in.

And if it is necessary also to bring in natural philosophy by the word, one might say, as before, that since the two are divided, and this is characteristic of matter, the number two is characteristic of the unclean. But also, the two being taken away, the Savior calls 'into one new man' (Ephesians 2:15) the two, both the one from circumcision and the one from the Gentiles, bringing them into the unity of the commonwealth according to the Gospel, which the ancient saints had, there being no difference between Hellenism and Judaism. For from the arts of which there are statues, and with them idolatry, and after them the law, Judaism comes to be. The first of the human commonwealths, which was Christianity, though it did not have this name, according to the common...

A common notion exists, which even the Savior proclaimed: 'Whatever you want that men should do to you, do likewise to them' (Matt 7:12). This lies in the common notion; for whatever one does not want to suffer, he ought not to do to his neighbor. Because of this, it lies in the common notion, so that the man being led by God may be without reproach.

Later, when the notion is perverted, the Scripture is given, not to fight against that, but to lead men into it; for it is said: 'The law was given for help' (Rom 7:12). So also the Gospel has been proclaimed in the whole world, so that no one might claim to be unreminded of common notions.

These things, then, are [treated] as regarding the literal [sense]; but it must also be said that clean animals are introduced seven times seven. For to say what follows the history, that because they are to be used by men both for sacred rites and for food, they must be more [numerous], and also because of the logic of numbers, since it is much remembered in the Scripture: I say, in the seventh [day], God ceased (Gen 2:2)... many.

For regarding the unbegotten, those around the week [refer to] the birth; for this is virgin and without a father and without a husband, so that the said thing may be such. All numbers within ten, being doubled or tripled, except the seven, beget and are begotten, such as one begetting two, and two the four, thus having been begotten by the one, and the four the eight having been begotten by the two; and the five the ten; but the six, whenever it begets, does not beget, and the seven is neither begotten by those who preceded it nor does it beget anyone by itself until ten; but also the two the six and the three the nine, being tripled, beget.

And it has another distinction; for if in a doubling logic you multiply the numbers from the unit up to seven, it becomes at once also a square; for one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two, having been doubled, becomes sixty-four, which is a square, for eight...

title: Divine Patience and Human Response
english: Eighty-six and sixty-four, a cube, for four times four is sixty-four. But also, being tripled up to seven from the unit, the seven hundred twenty-nine is formed, and being both a square and a cube: one, three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one, two hundred forty-three, seven hundred twenty-nine, as it has been said, completes both a cube and a square; thus the square: seventy-two times twenty-seven is seven hundred twenty-nine; thus the cube: nine times ninety-nine is seven hundred twenty-nine. The square signifies stability, but the cube [signifies something else].

Therefore, what has been spoken concerning the numbers would not be unrepresentative, having been proven by not involving the divine letters in nothing. And to those things spoken, it is appropriate to add that a porthole was appropriately left in the ark, so that, lest another origin arise, a heresy concerning two creators be introduced. For if, even with such security made, the heretics find differences, introducing divinities, how much more would they find plausible arguments for their own evil hypothesis.

For, 'And in seven days I will cause rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will destroy all the living things which I have made upon the face of the earth' (Genesis 7:4, 17). And this is foretold by the philanthropy of God for correction, in order to hear about the destruction that shall be after seven days, just as in the [disasters] we have set aside the preaching according to Jonah, which also happened through the repentance of the Ninevites, as it occurred. And forty days and forty nights of rain from above and below has happened in this way, so that the mountains were overwhelmed by fifty cubits.

If even the number according to which the destruction occurred has a reason, consider how 'I will destroy all the living things which I have made upon the face of the earth.' Some, having taken the [matter] of the destruction, thought that a previous world had endured a conflagration according to the Stoics, with the same [elements] existing in the matter which is unchangeable from this world. But this was sketched...
If in the demonstration of dogmas; for it is not possible for the movements of souls to occur without deviation from what has happened and what is to happen, so as to differ in no way.

Genesis 6:22: 'And Noah did all that the Lord God commanded him.' For all the things the Lord God commanded to be done are a testimony for man, and it is said in those things which preceded. The blessed David was also worthy of such an acceptance, concerning whom God said to find 'David the son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will do all my will' (Acts 13:22).

Genesis 6:3: 'And Noah was five hundred years old, and the flood of water came upon the earth.' ... [regarding] the goodness of God, how in a hundred percent of years he allowed the ark to be made; for this is evident from the five hundred years from when Noah began to ... it became wise toward the assembling of all things, so that seeing the strangeness of the construction, men might hear, learn the reason, and cease from wickedness. If they had heard and repented, the flood would not have come.

That this happened for the sake of long-suffering and to call men to repentance, Peter, the spokesman of the apostles, in the epistle concerning him, marks out concerning the Savior: 'In which also he went and preached to the spirits in prison, who indeed in the days of Noah, while the ark was being constructed, were disobedient, when the long-suffering of God was waiting' (1 Peter 3:19). And from this let us observe that he said many sins occur 'upon the earth' (Revelation 18:4); but God does not bring [the flood] ... for some reason of long-suffering, he makes this a place of repentance, giving [it]. So also, after a transgression, he gave a law that forbids, and after admonitions, he brings reproofs, not casting [them] away. And in the ... you will find this.

Israel, being part of the Lord and a son of God, transgressed his commands, even though God was doing all things for him. For what does he say in Isaiah? 'A horn was raised up for the beloved in a horn in a place of drinking' (Isaiah 49:2), where 'horn' refers to the kingship, and 'place of drinking' signifies the instruction through law and prophets. 'And...'
